title: Type A or Type B personality test: which are you? Free quiz — cv.cm
description: Free Type A personality test: rate 14 statements about hurry, competition and patience to see whether you lean Type A, Type B or a mix, with a score from 0 to 56 and tips. No sign-up; answers stay in your browser.
h1: Type A or Type B personality test
scoreLabel: Type A score (0 = Type B, 56 = Type A)
lede: Always racing the clock and keeping score, or happy to take life as it comes? Rate 14 statements to see whether you lean Type A, Type B or somewhere in between.
about: The Type A and Type B labels come from two American cardiologists, Meyer Friedman and Ray Rosenman, who in the 1950s noticed that many of their heart patients were driven, impatient and competitive, always in a hurry and quick to irritation. They called this Type A, and the more relaxed, easygoing pattern Type B. Later research found that the pattern as a whole predicts heart disease less well than first thought; the hostility and anger part seems to matter most. The labels stuck anyway, because many people recognize themselves in them.

The statements here were written for cv.cm around the classic signs of the pattern: time urgency, doing several things at once, competitiveness, impatience and finding it hard to relax. They are not the Jenkins Activity Survey or any other published questionnaire, and half of them describe Type B, so agreeing with everything lands in the middle. Most people are a mix, so read your score as a tendency, not a fixed type, and not as anything to do with your health.

faq.q: What is a Type A personality?
faq.a: A pattern of being driven, competitive and always in a hurry: you juggle tasks, hate waiting, measure yourself by what you get done and find it hard to switch off.

faq.q: What is a Type B personality?
faq.a: The opposite pattern: relaxed, patient and less competitive. Type B people can still work hard and succeed; they just feel less pressure from the clock.

faq.q: How is the score worked out?
faq.a: Each statement scores 0 to 4, and the Type B statements are reversed, so the total runs from 0 to 56. 18 or less leans Type B, 19 to 37 is a mix and 38 or more leans Type A.

faq.q: Is being Type A bad for your heart?
faq.a: The overall pattern turned out to be a weak predictor. Frequent anger and hostility seem to matter more, along with the usual risks such as smoking and blood pressure. If your health worries you, talk to a doctor; this quiz can't tell you anything about your heart.

items: I often feel there aren't enough hours in the day.
I can relax without feeling guilty about it.
Waiting in a queue makes me impatient fast.
I don't mind much when someone else wins.
I often do two or three things at once.
I eat, walk and talk at an unhurried pace.
I get irritated when other people work too slowly.
I judge my day by how much I got done.
I can leave work unfinished and still enjoy my evening.
I turn even friendly games into a competition.
I stay patient when people keep me waiting.
I find it hard to sit and do nothing.

typeb.name: Leaning Type B (0–18)
typeb.body: You're relaxed, patient and not too bothered about the clock or the scoreboard. You can switch off, enjoy the moment and let small delays go, which is good for you and for the people around you. If you ever feel you drift, a simple plan for the things that matter most can add drive without the stress.

mixed.name: A mix of Type A and B (19–37)
mixed.body: You have both sides: driven and competitive when something matters, relaxed when it doesn't. That's where most people land, and it's a useful balance. Notice which situations bring out your Type A side, such as work, deadlines or traffic, and whether you'd like to keep it there.

typea.name: Leaning Type A (38–56)
typea.body: You're driven, fast and competitive, and you get a lot done. That energy is a strength, but the hurry and impatience can wear you out and strain your relationships. Try building in real breaks, doing one thing at a time, and noticing when irritation flares: it's the part of Type A most worth taming.
